overgo evidence conditioning: a change proposed with and without the past verdicts of its corpus's runs
tool: cmd/train -propose <corpus> -pool <acceptance> -proposal <directory> [-evidence [-evidence-to-sequence N] [-evidence-max-bytes B]] (trainingworkflow.ProposeChange), built from commit 685397181 with this change
corpus: evidence:sha256:aa99fadce714d52bd87e66f3d8d762dc20ccf1f4e9cdf23fa8f20defa51794d1 (docs/verification/change-corpus-qwen25-05b.txt: 24 fine-tunes of Qwen2.5-0.5B)
pool: evidence:sha256:712b094e89d103f1fe2eafafc68c2b8f4e2fc0608ec0f714b04f13dd5f8df49b, the acceptance of a held-out pool of the corpus's objective built in the experiment store for this comparison (cmd/training-objective -pool, gain 0.5, weights 1, 2, 6 and 2): 21, 32, 92 and 27 documents in its development, selection, promotion and audit parts, none of them a document the corpus's verdicts read
store: the experiment store the corpus was collected in, overgo_data/experiments/change-corpus/store
flags: -seq 512, the corpus runs' sequence length; each arm's candidates written under the corpus's runs directory, in pool-none, pool-now and pool-cutoff
measure: the mean log-likelihood of a document's tokens, each predicted from the ones before it; larger is better

what an arm is shown and what it does with it
  the proposer reads each run's gain over the base on the 21 documents of the pool's development part and fits its code to those gains. That is all the arm shown nothing has.
  an arm shown held-out verdicts takes those that judged a run of its corpus. Each records what the run and its base scored on the 24 records the run was judged on when it was trained, in token accuracy. The gains the verdicts record are fitted beside the pool's: each kind taken about its mean in units of its spread over the runs it covers, and the two added; a run no shown verdict judged keeps its pool gain alone.
  the verdicts of the store as it stands and of the store as it stood are named by evaluation.PastHeldoutVerdicts, the second through a journal sequence and under a bound on the bytes named. As it stands the store holds 32, the corpus's 24 and 8 of other objectives that the store was copied with, which bear on no run of the corpus. At sequence 78600 it held those 8 and the first 16 of the corpus's.
  every candidate is scored on the 32 documents of the pool's selection part. An arm shown verdicts also scores the proposal the same code makes of the pool's gains alone, which is the first arm's proposal weight for weight, and bounds its own proposal's score less that one's over ten thousand redraws of the selection documents.

what it shows
  the evidence does not measurably improve what the proposer proposes. Shown every verdict of its corpus's runs, its proposal scores 0.0016 above the proposal without them, and the middle of the redrawn differences runs from below zero to above it; shown two thirds of them, the same. The step's rule was that no benefit is a valid outcome and closes it.
  the two arms shown verdicts differ in what they were shown, 24 runs judged against 16 and 28,698 bytes against 21,525, and not in what came of it: their proposals score the same to four places.
  in every arm the plain mean of the 24 runs is the best candidate and the proposal is not kept: it scores 0.031 to 0.033 below the mean, and the middle nineteen parts in twenty of the redrawn differences lie wholly below zero. That is what the earlier judgment of this corpus found on the records its runs were judged on (docs/verification/change-proposal-qwen25-05b.txt); here it is found on documents no run and no verdict read. The runs' pool gains spread no further than the noise of one run's gain, so there is little in them for a direction to be fitted to, with the evidence or without.
  not shown here: whether evidence helps a proposer whose runs do differ in gain by more than the measurement's noise, or one that chooses which runs to make. A learned encoder of experiment records was not built, as the step said it would not be unless the plain reader fell short of something measurable; nothing here says it would do better.
